threshold: Parameters, selection rule and staking rule are committed to the repo and timestamped before any graded result is recorded.
why: Anything tuned after seeing results is hindsight, not skill.

threshold: At least 200 graded bets at the declared unit size.
why: Below roughly this sample the confidence interval on ROI is wider than any plausible edge.

threshold: Graded only on results dated after the pre-registration timestamp.
why: In-sample performance does not predict out-of-sample performance.

threshold: Modelled edge must exceed the book's overround on the relevant market.
why: Beating a number that already contains the margin is the only definition of profitable.

threshold: Two-sided test of hit rate against the implied break-even probability; nominal p below 0.05.
why: Separates a real edge from a run of luck.

threshold: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 10% applied within the declared strategy family.
why: With many strategies, naive p-values manufacture winners.

threshold: The 5th percentile of a bet-level bootstrap of ROI is above zero.
why: Guards against a result carried by a handful of outliers.

threshold: Edge remains positive across the full pre-declared parameter neighbourhood, not only at the fitted point.
why: A sharp optimum is usually a fitted artefact.

threshold: The line was actually obtainable at the recorded price for the declared stake.
why: A price you cannot get is not an edge.

threshold: Edge is not concentrated in a single season-week or a single team.
why: Concentration means the signal is really one event, not a strategy.

threshold: Every input row used by the signal carries a fetch timestamp earlier than kickoff.
why: A signal built on post-kickoff data is not tradeable.

threshold: Every parlay or prop combo declares its estimated leg correlation and the estimator's fit window.
